24.t: probe would be placed on the pin which is used to control when the data will be entered; in this case it is the shift load input (S/L) at pin 1. When the shift load pin goes low, the information will be loaded into the register. Then take the second probe and check the ROM address inputs and compare these with the information at the multiplexer inputs. Finally, compare ali of this information with the table.

2-88. For example, first check ROM address ao (pin 15) with the second probe and you should see a high pulse occurring at the same time as the low shift load pulse, Note that this correctly corresponds to the ROM address table. Then look at AY {pin 8) and again there should be a high pulse occurring simultaneously with the low shift load pulse. Now go to A® and you should see signal 103 which will pulse high and low as the steering wheel is rotated, Continue to check all the address inputs in the same fashion. If you find some information which does not correctly correspond, start checking back through the multiplexers and gates (if any). If all the information checks out OK, examine the component that information is being loaded into (shift register F6 in this case).

2-89. To troubleshoot the multiplexers, first check the multiplexer inputs. if any of these do not check out, go to the section which produces the malfunctioning signal and locate the malfunction there. However, if all the multiplexer inputs are OK, check the data select lines by going to gates H3 and L5 and verifying the presence of the correct
103-7 Ld1B, VLd1, 512H and SCORE DISP inputs. If all of the data select inputs are also OK, you must check the multiplexers themselves.

2-90, The multiplexers are most easily checked using a logic comparator {see paragraph 1-11). The comparator will yield fast and accurate results. If you do not have a comparator, use the following procedure: first tie both multiplexer select lines low and look at the information from pins 7 and 9 {multiplexed outputs) which must match the inputs at pins 6 and 10 (multiplexer inputs). If OK, tie Sy high and So low, and pins 7 and 9 should match § and 11. If OK here, tie Sy low and $y high, and 7 and 9 should equal 4 and 12. To check the last set, tie both select lines high and pins 7 and 9 should match 3 and 13,
